questions.prompt: How often do you use social media?
questions.sampleA1: I use social media. Every day. I like it.
questions.sampleA2: I use social media every day. I like to see photos of my friends and family. But sometimes it is boring. And I don't like the news.
questions.sampleB1: I use social media quite a lot, I think. Probably every day, maybe for an hour or two. I like to see what my friends are doing, and also to follow some interesting pages. However, sometimes I think I spend too much time on it. So I try to use it less.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'm on social media pretty much all the time — I'd say I check it dozens of times a day. It's the first thing I reach for in the morning. I mainly scroll through Instagram and Telegram to keep up with friends and catch up on the news. I suppose I spend too long on it, but I can't really help it.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan foydalanaman. Har kuni. Menga yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men har kuni ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan foydalanaman. Menga do'stlarim va oilamning rasmlarini ko'rish yoqadi. Lekin ba'zida zerikarli bo'ladi. Va yangiliklarni yoqtirmayman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan juda ko'p foydalanaman, deb o'ylayman. Ehtimol, har kuni, balki bir-ikki soat. Menga do'stlarim nima qilayotganini ko'rish yoqadi, shuningdek, ba'zi qiziqarli sahifalarni kuzatib boraman.
Biroq, ba'zida men unga juda ko'p vaqt sarflayotganimni o'ylayman. Shuning uchun men undan kamroq foydalanishga harakat qilaman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Menimcha, ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan yetarlicha muntazam foydalanaman, balki kuniga bir necha marta. Bu do'stlar va oila a'zolari bilan aloqada bo'lishning qulay usuli, ayniqsa, uzoqda yashaydiganlar bilan. Shuningdek, undan yangiliklarni kuzatib borish va yangi narsalar haqida bilib olish uchun foydalanaman. Biroq, men noto'g'ri ma'lumotlarning tarqalishi va ushbu platformalarning o'rganib qolish xususiyati kabi potentsial kamchiliklardan xabardorman. Shuning uchun, men iste'mol qiladigan narsalarimni juda tanlab olishga va ijtimoiy tarmoqlarda vaqtimni cheklashga harakat qilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - How often do you use social media?
sentenceStarters: "I use social media quite frequently, especially..." - "Men ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan juda tez-tez foydalanaman, ayniqsa..."
"To be honest, I spend a lot of time on..." - "Rostini aytsam, men ko'p vaqtimni ... ga sarflayman..."
"I try to limit my social media use because..." - "Men ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan foydalanishni cheklashga harakat qilaman, chunki..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I use social media quite frequently, I'd say several times a day. It's become an integral part of my daily routine, whether I'm checking updates from friends or staying informed about current events.
I primarily use platforms like Instagram and Telegram. Instagram is great for visual content and keeping up with friends' lives, while Telegram helps me stay connected with various groups and channels related to my interests and work.
However, I try to be mindful about my usage. It's easy to get sucked into endless scrolling, so I've set time limits on my phone. As the saying goes, "Everything in moderation." I believe social media is a useful tool, but it shouldn't take over your life.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan juda tez-tez foydalanaman, kuniga bir necha marta desam ham bo'ladi. Bu mening kundalik hayotimning ajralmas qismiga aylandi, do'stlarimdan yangiliklarni tekshiramanmi yoki dolzarb voqealar haqida xabardor bo'lamanmi, farqi yo'q.

Men asosan Instagram va Telegram kabi platformalardan foydalanaman. Instagram vizual kontent uchun va do'stlarimning hayotidan xabardor bo'lib turish uchun juda yaxshi, Telegram esa menga o'z qiziqishlarim va ishim bilan bog'liq turli guruhlar va kanallar bilan aloqada bo'lishga yordam beradi.

Biroq, men foydalanishimga e'tiborli bo'lishga harakat qilaman. Cheksiz varaqlashga berilib ketish oson, shuning uchun telefonimda vaqt chegaralarini o'rnatdim. Maqol bor, "Har narsada me'yor bo'lishi kerak". Men ijtimoiy tarmoqlar foydali vosita deb hisoblayman, lekin u sizning hayotingizni egallab olmasligi kerak.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer texting or calling people?
questions.sampleA1: I like texting. It is easy. I text my friends.
questions.sampleA2: I like texting more. Because it is easy. And I can text my friends. But calling is okay too sometimes.
questions.sampleB1: I prefer texting people. I think it's easier than calling. For example, if I need to ask a quick question, I will text. However, if it's something important, maybe I will call them. It depends.
questions.sampleB2: The thing is, it depends on who I'm talking to. For everyday stuff, I prefer texting — you can fire off a quick message and get back to it whenever suits you. But when it comes to something personal or a bit tricky, I'd rather pick up the phone. You can pick up on someone's tone straight away, and that saves a lot of misunderstandings.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga xabar yozish yoqadi. Bu oson. Men do'stlarimga xabar yozaman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menga ko'proq xabar yozish yoqadi. Chunki bu oson. Va men do'stlarimga xabar yoza olaman. Lekin qo'ng'iroq qilish ham ba'zida yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men odamlarga xabar yozishni afzal ko'raman. O'ylashimcha, bu qo'ng'iroq qilishdan osonroq.
Misol uchun, agar menga tezda biror narsa so'rash kerak bo'lsa, men xabar yozaman.
Biroq, agar bu muhimroq narsa bo'lsa, ehtimol ularga qo'ng'iroq qilaman. Bu vaziyatga bog'liq.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men ko'p hollarda qo'ng'iroq qilishdan ko'ra, xabar yozishga moyilman deb o'ylayman. Xabar yozish menga boshqa odamning gapini bo'lmasdan samarali muloqot qilish imkonini beradi. Bundan tashqari, suhbatning yozuvini saqlab qolish uchun ham foydali.
Shunga qaramay, murakkabroq yoki nozikroq muhokamalar uchun telefon qo'ng'irog'i ancha yaxshiroq deb bilaman. Siz ohang va his-tuyg'ularni osonroq yetkazishingiz mumkin, bu esa tushunmovchiliklarning oldini olish uchun muhimdir.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do you prefer texting or calling people?
sentenceStarters: "I generally prefer texting because..." - "Men odatda SMS yozishni afzal ko'raman, chunki..."
"It really depends on the situation, but..." - "Bu haqiqatan ham vaziyatga bog'liq, lekin..."
"For important conversations, I prefer..." - "Muhim suhbatlar uchun men ... ni afzal ko'raman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I would say I generally prefer texting over calling, though it really depends on the situation and the person I'm communicating with.
Texting is more convenient for quick exchanges and when I don't want to disturb someone. I can respond at my own pace and have time to think about what I want to say. It's also useful for sharing links, photos, or information that would be difficult to convey over the phone.
However, for important matters or emotional conversations, I definitely prefer calling or even meeting face-to-face. There's something about hearing someone's voice that makes communication more personal and genuinely meaningful. As they say, "The tone of voice can say more than words." You can't always pick up on emotions through text.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men odatda qo'ng'iroq qilishdan ko'ra xabar yozishni afzal ko'raman, deb aytgan bo'lardim, garchi bu vaziyatga va men muloqot qilayotgan odamga bog'liq.

Xabar yozish tezkor almashinuvlar uchun va kimnidir bezovta qilishni xohlamaganimda qulayroq. Men o'z tezligimda javob bera olaman va nima demoqchiligim haqida o'ylab ko'rishga vaqtim bor. Bundan tashqari, telefon orqali yetkazish qiyin bo'lgan havolalar, fotosuratlar yoki ma'lumotlarni baham ko'rish uchun ham foydali.

Biroq, muhim masalalar yoki hissiy suhbatlar uchun men qo'ng'iroq qilishni yoki hatto yuzma-yuz uchrashishni afzal ko'raman. Kimningdir ovozini eshitishda muloqotni shaxsiylashtiradigan va chinakam ma'noli qiladigan nimadir bor. Aytishlaricha, "Ovoz ohangi so'zlardan ko'ra ko'proq narsani aytishi mumkin". Siz har doim ham matn orqali his-tuyg'ularni ilg'ay olmaysiz.

questions.prompt: What gadget or device could you not live without?
questions.sampleA1:
My phone.

I like phone.

Use it every day.
questions.sampleA2:
I think my phone is important.

I use it for calls and messages.

And I listen to music on it.

I can't live without it, because it's very useful.
questions.sampleB1:
I think the gadget I couldn't live without is my laptop.

I use it for everything, like studying and watching videos.

Also, I need it for writing emails and doing homework.

It's very important for my studies and entertainment, so I would be lost without it.
questions.sampleB2: Honestly, I couldn't get by without my smartphone — it's practically glued to my hand. I use it for everything: waking up, finding my way around, paying for things, you name it. I suppose the one I'd really struggle without, though, is my wireless earbuds. They let me zone out and focus wherever I am, which is a lifesaver on a noisy commute.

Mening telefonim.

Telefon menga yoqadi.

Har kuni undan foydalanaman.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menimcha, telefonim muhim.

Men undan qo'ng'iroqlar va xabarlar uchun foydalanaman.

Men usiz yashay olmayman, chunki u juda foydali.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, men yashay olmasligim mumkin bo'lgan gadjet bu mening noutbukim.

Men undan hamma narsa uchun foydalanaman, masalan, o'qish va videolarni tomosha qilish uchun.

questions.uzSampleB2:
Xo'sh, agar tanlashim kerak bo'lsa, shovqinni bekor qiluvchi quloqchinlarim men haqiqatan ham ularsiz yashay olmaydigan yagona gadjet deb aytgan bo'lardim.

Men ulardan doimiy ravishda foydalanaman, ayniqsa, shovqinli muhitda ish yoki o'qishga e'tibor qaratmoqchi bo'lganimda.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - What gadget could you not live without?
idioms: you don't know what you've got until it's gone - "yo'qotmaguncha qadriga yetmayman"
sentenceStarters: "Without a doubt, the device I couldn't live without is..." - "Shubhasiz, men holsiz qila olmaydigan qurilma..."
"My smartphone has become essential because..." - "Mening smartfonim muhim bo'lib qoldi, chunki..."
"I rely on this device for..." - "Men bu qurilmaga ... uchun tayanaman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Without a doubt, my smartphone is the one device I absolutely could not live without. It has become an essential tool that I rely on for virtually every aspect of my daily life.
My phone serves multiple purposes – it's my alarm clock, my camera, my music player, my navigation system, and my connection to the world. I use it for communication, work, entertainment, and even banking. It's incredibly convenient to have all these functions in one pocket-sized device.
I remember once when my phone broke, and I felt completely lost for a few days! It made me realize how dependent we've become on technology. As the saying goes, "You don't know what you've got until it's gone." While this dependency might be concerning, the convenience my smartphone provides is truly unmatched.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Shubhasiz, mening smartfonim мен mutlaqo yashay olmaydigan yagona qurilma. U mening kundalik hayotimning deyarli har bir jabhasida tayanishim mumkin bo'lgan muhim vositaga aylandi.

Mening telefonim bir nechta maqsadlarga xizmat qiladi – u mening budilnikim, kameram, musiqa pleyerim, navigatsiya tizimim va dunyo bilan aloqam. Men undan aloqa, ish, ko'ngil ochish va hatto bank operatsiyalari uchun foydalanaman. Barcha funksiyalarning bitta cho'ntak o'lchamidagi qurilmada bo'lishi juda qulay.

Esimda, bir marta telefonim buzilib qolganida, bir necha kun o'zimni butunlay yo'qotgandek his qilgandim! Bu bizning texnologiyaga qanchalik bog'lanib qolganimizni anglatdi. Aytishlaricha, "Bor narsangni yo'qotmaguningcha qadriga yetmaysan". Bu qaramlik xavotirli bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, mening smartfonim taqdim etadigan qulaylik haqiqatan ham beqiyosdir.

questions.prompt: Compare these two pictures showing different ways people communicate.
questions.sampleA1:
This is people talk.

This is phone.

I like talk.
questions.sampleA2:
One picture is people talking.

And the other is people with phones.

The people with phones are not talking.

I think talking is good.
questions.sampleB1:
The pictures show different ways to communicate.

In one picture, people are talking to each other. It looks like they are having a good time.

But in the other picture, everyone is using their phone.

I think it's better to talk to people in person, however, phones are also important.
questions.sampleB2: Well, both pictures show people communicating, but in different settings. In the first, a man and a woman are sitting across a table, having a face-to-face chat — it looks like a meeting or an interview. She's smiling and they're making eye contact, so there's a real sense of connection. In the second picture, a young woman is curled up on her sofa, waving and smiling at her phone — she's on a video call. To be honest, both are valid ways to keep in touch, but the first feels warmer and more personal, while the second is more convenient.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Birinchi rasmda odamlar gaplashyapti.

Va ikkinchi rasmda odamlar telefon bilan.

Telefonli odamlar gaplashmayapti.

Menimcha, gaplashish yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Rasmlarda odamlarning muloqot qilishning turli usullari ko'rsatilgan.

Bir rasmda odamlar bir-biri bilan gaplashmoqda. Ularning vaqti yaxshi o'tayotganga o'xshaydi.

Ammo boshqa rasmda hamma telefonidan foydalanmoqda.

Menimcha, odamlar bilan yuzma-yuz gaplashish yaxshiroq, ammo telefonlar ham muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Bu ikki rasm muloqotning qarama-qarshi usullarini ko'rsatadi.

Birinchisi, odamlarning yuzma-yuz muloqot qilishini, qizg'in suhbatga kirishganini ko'rsatadi. Aloqa va umumiy tajriba hissi bor.

Ikkinchi rasmda bir guruh odamlar smartfonlariga berilib, bir-biriga e'tibor bermayotgani tasvirlangan.

Texnologiya ko'plab afzalliklarni taqdim etsa va tezkor aloqaga imkon bersa-da, u yaqin atrofdagilardan ajralish va begonalashuv hissiga ham olib kelishi mumkin. Muloqotning bu ikki shakli o'rtasida muvozanatni topish muhim.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - Compare these two pictures...
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I can see people..." - "Birinchi rasmda men odamlarni ... ko'ryapman..."
"The second image shows a completely different..." - "Ikkinchi rasm butunlay boshqacha ... ko'rsatmoqda..."
"These pictures illustrate the contrast between..." - "Bu rasmlar ... o'rtasidagi farqni ko'rsatadi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
These two pictures present a striking contrast between two different approaches to human communication in today's world.
In the first image, we can see people engaged in face-to-face conversation. They appear to be genuinely connected, making eye contact and actively listening to each other. There's a warmth and personal connection visible in their interaction. The atmosphere seems relaxed and engaging, with people fully present in the moment.
The second picture shows a completely different scenario – people who are physically together but each absorbed in their own smartphone. Despite being in the same space, they seem disconnected from each other, focused on their screens rather than the people around them. This has become an increasingly common sight in our digital age.
These images effectively illustrate how technology has changed the way we interact. While smartphones keep us connected to the wider world, they can sometimes create barriers to meaningful connection with those physically present. As they say, "We are connected to everyone but connected to no one."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki rasm bugungi kunda insonlar o'rtasidagi muloqotning ikki xil usulini o'rtaga tashlab, keskin farqni ko'rsatib beradi.

Birinchi rasmda biz odamlarning yuzma-yuz suhbatlashayotganini ko'rishimiz mumkin. Ular chin dildan bog'langan, bir-biriga ko'z uzmay va faol tinglayotgandek ko'rinadi. Ularning o'zaro munosabatlarida iliqlik va shaxsiy aloqa seziladi. Atmosfera xotirjam va qiziqarli, odamlar butunlay shu lahzada hozirdek.

Ikkinchi rasm butunlay boshqa vaziyatni ko'rsatadi – odamlar jismonan birga, lekin har biri o'z smartfoniga berilib ketgan. Bir xil joyda bo'lishiga qaramay, ular atrofidagilarga emas, balki ekranlariga e'tibor qaratib, bir-biridan uzilgandek tuyuladi. Bu bizning raqamli davrimizda tobora keng tarqalgan manzara bo'lib qoldi.

Bu rasmlar texnologiyaning bizning o'zaro munosabatlarimizni qanday o'zgartirganini samarali tarzda ko'rsatib beradi. Smartfonlar bizni keng dunyo bilan bog'lab tursa-da, ular ba'zan jismonan hozir bo'lganlar bilan mazmunli aloqa o'rnatishga to'siqlar yaratishi mumkin. Aytishlaricha, "Biz hamma bilan bog'langanmiz, lekin hech kim bilan bog'lanmaganmiz".

I suppose that's why it's so much easier to build trust and really connect with someone when you're sitting right in front of them.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the benefits of face-to-face communication?
idioms: the eyes are the window to the soul - "ko'zlar ruhning oynasi"
sentenceStarters: "One of the main benefits is..." - "Asosiy afzalliklardan biri..."
"Face-to-face communication allows us to..." - "Yuzma-yuz muloqot bizga ... imkonini beradi..."
"In-person conversations are valuable because..." - "Shaxsan suhbatlar qimmatli, chunki..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Face-to-face communication offers numerous significant benefits that digital communication simply cannot replicate.
Firstly, and most importantly, in-person conversations allow us to read body language and facial expressions. Research suggests that over 70% of communication is non-verbal. A smile, a frown, or a gesture can convey meaning that words alone cannot express. This makes conversations richer and helps avoid misunderstandings.
Secondly, face-to-face interaction builds stronger emotional bonds. When we're physically present with someone, we can offer a comforting hug, share a laugh, or simply enjoy each other's company. These shared experiences create lasting memories and deepen relationships.
Additionally, in-person communication demands our full attention. There are no notifications to distract us, no other chats to check. This focused attention makes the other person feel valued and respected.
Furthermore, important discussions – whether business negotiations or personal matters – are often more effective face-to-face. Trust is built more easily when you can look someone in the eye. As the proverb says, "The eyes are the window to the soul."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Yuzma-yuz muloqot raqamli muloqot takrorlay olmaydigan ko'plab muhim afzalliklarni taqdim etadi.

Birinchidan, va eng muhimi, shaxsan suhbatlar bizga tana tilini va yuz ifodalarini o'qishga imkon beradi. Tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, muloqotning 70% dan ortig'i og'zaki bo'lmagan holda amalga oshiriladi. Tabassum, qovog'ini solish yoki imo-ishora so'zlar bilan ifodalab bo'lmaydigan ma'noni anglatishi mumkin. Bu suhbatlarni yanada boy qiladi va tushunmovchiliklarning oldini olishga yordam beradi.

Ikkinchidan, yuzma-yuz muloqot kuchliroq hissiy bog'lanishlarni yaratadi. Biz kimdir bilan jismonan birga bo'lganimizda, biz tasalli beruvchi quchoq taklif qilishimiz, birgalikda kulishimiz yoki shunchaki bir-birimizning kompaniyamizdan zavqlanishimiz mumkin. Ushbu birgalikdagi tajribalar uzoq muddatli xotiralarni yaratadi va munosabatlarni chuqurlashtiradi.

Bundan tashqari, shaxsan muloqot bizning to'liq e'tiborimizni talab qiladi. Bizni chalg'itadigan bildirishnomalar yo'q, tekshirish uchun boshqa chatlar yo'q. Ushbu diqqat markazlashgan e'tibor boshqa odamni qadrlanadigan va hurmat qilinadigan his qiladi.

Bundan tashqari, muhim muhokamalar - biznes muzokaralari yoki shaxsiy masalalar bo'ladimi - ko'pincha yuzma-yuz samaraliroq bo'ladi. Kimningdir ko'ziga qaray olganingizda ishonch osonroq shakllanadi. Maqolda aytilganidek, "Ko'zlar - ruhning oynasi".

What's more, shy or introverted people often feel more at ease writing things out, since they've got time to think before they reply. And phones let you stay in touch with people who live miles away, which is a huge plus.

Shunga qaramay, men ba'zida odamlar bilan yuzma-yuz gaplashishni ham yoqtiraman.

Birinchi sabab qulaylik; uchrashuv tashkil qilishdan ko'ra tezkor xabar yuborish ancha oson. Bundan tashqari, bu sizga suhbat yozuvini saqlash imkonini beradi. Biroq, menimcha, kuchliroq munosabatlar o'rnatish uchun yuzma-yuz muloqot qilish hali ham muhim.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why might some people prefer communicating through phones?
idioms: different strokes for different folks - "har kim o'z yo'lini tanlaydi"
"At the touch of a button" - "Bir tugma bosish bilan"
sentenceStarters: "Many people prefer phone communication because..." - "Ko'p odamlar telefon orqali muloqotni afzal ko'rishadi, chunki..."
"For some individuals, texting is easier because..." - "Ba'zi odamlar uchun xabar yozish osonroq, chunki..."
"Digital communication offers advantages like..." - "Raqamli aloqa ... kabi afzalliklarni taklif qiladi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several valid reasons why many people today prefer digital communication over face-to-face interaction.
Firstly, phone communication offers unmatched convenience and flexibility. You can send a message anytime, anywhere, without worrying about whether the other person is available. This is particularly useful for people with busy schedules or those in different time zones.
Secondly, some people feel more comfortable expressing themselves through text. Introverted individuals, for example, may find face-to-face conversations draining or anxiety-inducing. Texting gives them time to think and compose their thoughts without the pressure of immediate response.
Additionally, digital communication creates a written record. Important information, addresses, or instructions can be saved and referenced later. You can't do that with a spoken conversation.
Furthermore, phones allow us to stay connected with people who are physically far away. Thanks to messaging apps and video calls, we can maintain relationships across continents. For the younger generation who grew up with technology, digital communication feels as natural as breathing. As they say, "Different strokes for different folks."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bugungi kunda ko'pchilikning yuzma-yuz muloqotdan ko'ra raqamli aloqani afzal ko'rishining bir nechta asosli sabablari bor.

Birinchidan, telefon orqali aloqa misli ko'rilmagan qulaylik va moslashuvchanlikni ta'minlaydi. Siz xohlagan vaqtda, xohlagan joyda, boshqa odamning band yoki band emasligidan xavotirlanmasdan xabar yuborishingiz mumkin. Bu, ayniqsa, band jadvalga ega yoki turli vaqt mintaqalarida bo'lgan odamlar uchun foydalidir.

Ikkinchidan, ba'zi odamlar o'z fikrlarini matn orqali ifoda etishda o'zlarini qulayroq his qilishadi. Misol uchun, introvert shaxslar yuzma-yuz suhbatlarni charchatuvchi yoki xavotirga soluvchi deb bilishlari mumkin. SMS yozish ularga o'ylash va o'z fikrlarini darhol javob berish bosimisiz yozib olishga vaqt beradi.

Bundan tashqari, raqamli aloqa yozma yozuv yaratadi. Muhim ma'lumotlar, manzillar yoki ko'rsatmalarni saqlash va keyinroq ularga murojaat qilish mumkin. Og'zaki suhbatda buni qila olmaysiz.

Bundan tashqari, telefonlar bizga jismonan uzoqda bo'lgan odamlar bilan aloqada bo'lishimizga imkon beradi. Xabar almashish ilovalari va video qo'ng'iroqlar tufayli biz qit'alar bo'ylab munosabatlarni saqlab qolishimiz mumkin. Texnologiya bilan o'sgan yosh avlod uchun raqamli aloqa nafas olish kabi tabiiy tuyuladi. Aytishlaricha, "Har kimning o'z didi bor".

questions.prompt: Describe a time when technology helped you solve a problem.
questions.sampleA1: I have problem. My phone... no work. I ask friend. Friend help me. Phone okay now.
questions.sampleA2: One time I needed help with my homework. It was math. I used the internet. I found the answer and I understood it. It was good because I finished my homework.
questions.sampleB1: I remember once when I had a problem with my computer. It was very slow, and I didn't know why. I searched on Google for solutions. I found a video that explained how to clean up my computer. I followed the instructions, and it worked! My computer is much faster now. I think the internet is very useful.
questions.sampleB2: Right, let me tell you about a time technology really got me out of a tight spot. It was about a year ago, when I was travelling to Istanbul for the very first time for a conference. The problem was that I landed late in the evening, jumped in a taxi, and only realised halfway there that I had no idea where my hotel actually was. To make matters worse, the driver didn't speak a word of English, my paper booking had the address in the wrong district, and my phone battery was hovering at about five percent. I was starting to panic, to be honest. Luckily, this is where technology came to the rescue. Before my battery gave out completely, I quickly opened up Google Maps and downloaded an offline version of the city. I typed in the hotel name, and it gave me the exact location along with step-by-step directions. I showed the map to the driver, and straight away he knew where to go. On top of that, I used a translation app to type out a quick message in Turkish, just so we could sort out the fare without any confusion. Within about fifteen minutes, we pulled up right outside my hotel, and I could finally breathe a sigh of relief. Looking back, that little episode really brought home just how much we rely on technology these days. Without a smartphone and a bit of battery, I honestly don't know what I would have done. Ever since then, I always make a point of downloading offline maps and carrying a power bank whenever I travel — you can never be too careful.

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd like to share an experience from last year when technology literally saved my trip abroad.
The problem was that I got completely lost in an unfamiliar city. I had arrived in Istanbul for a conference, and my hotel was in a neighborhood with confusing streets. My printed map was useless, and nobody around spoke English. To make matters worse, my phone's battery was dying, and I had no idea where to find my hotel.
Thankfully, technology came to my rescue. I quickly downloaded an offline map before my battery died completely. Google Maps showed me the exact route to my hotel, with step-by-step directions. It even worked without internet! Additionally, I used a translation app to ask a local shopkeeper for directions, and he kindly pointed me in the right direction.
I felt incredibly relieved and grateful when I finally reached my hotel. This experience made me appreciate how technology can be a lifesaver in difficult situations. It taught me to always be prepared – now I always download offline maps and carry a portable charger. As they say, "Technology is best when it brings people together" – or in my case, brings people to their hotels!
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men o'tgan yildagi, texnologiya mening xorijiy sayohatimni tom ma'noda qutqargan bir voqeani baham ko'rmoqchiman.

Muammo shundaki, men notanish shaharda butunlay adashib qoldim. Men Istanbulga konferensiya uchun kelgandim va mehmonxonam chalkash ko'chalari bo'lgan mahallada joylashgan edi. Mening bosma xaritam foydasiz edi va atrofimdagi hech kim ingliz tilida gapirmasdi. Vaziyatni yanada og'irlashtiradigan narsa, telefonim batareyasi o'chib borayotgan edi va men mehmonxonamni qayerdan topishni bilmasdim.

Yaxshiyamki, texnologiya yordamga keldi. Batareyam butunlay o'chib qolishidan oldin, men tezda oflayn xaritani yuklab oldim. Google Maps menga mehmonxonamga aniq yo'nalishni, qadam-baqadam ko'rsatmalar bilan ko'rsatdi. U hatto internetsiz ham ishladi! Bundan tashqari, men mahalliy do'kondordan yo'l so'rash uchun tarjima ilovasidan foydalandim va u menga to'g'ri yo'nalishni ko'rsatdi.

Men nihoyat mehmonxonamga yetib kelganimda, o'zimni juda xotirjam va minnatdor his qildim. Bu tajriba menga texnologiyaning qiyin vaziyatlarda qanday qutqaruvchi bo'lishi mumkinligini anglashga yordam berdi. Bu menga doimo tayyor bo'lishni o'rgatdi – endi men har doim oflayn xaritalarni yuklab olaman va portativ zaryadlovchi olib yuraman. Aytishlaricha, "Texnologiya odamlarni birlashtirganda eng yaxshisidir" – yoki mening holatimda, odamlarni o'z mehmonxonalariga olib boradi!

questions.prompt: Children Under 12 Should Not Have Their Own Smartphones
questions.sampleA1: I think no. Phone is for big people. Kids play.
questions.sampleA2: I think no, because phones are expensive. And kids can break them. But maybe if they are good, they can have one.
questions.sampleB1: I think that children under 12 probably shouldn't have smartphones. They are very young, and they might spend too much time on them. Also, there are a lot of bad things on the internet, and it's hard for parents to watch everything. However, it can be useful for parents to contact their kids.
questions.sampleB2: This is a really divisive topic, and I can genuinely see where both sides are coming from. On the one hand, there's a strong case for keeping smartphones out of young children's hands. For a start, kids under twelve are pretty vulnerable, and giving them unrestricted access to the internet can expose them to all sorts of inappropriate content. On top of that, there's the risk of cyberbullying, which can really take a toll on a child's mental health. And let's be honest, spending hours hooked on a screen at such a young age can eat into their sleep, their studies, and playing outdoors with friends. Some experts even argue it can hold back their social skills. On the other hand, I do think smartphones have their upsides. For many parents, being able to reach their child at the drop of a hat gives them real peace of mind, especially with features like location tracking. A phone can also be a brilliant learning tool if it's used sensibly. At the end of the day, though, I'd come down on the side of holding off. In my view, the answer isn't a flat ban, but rather a sensible middle ground. If a child does need a phone, I'd say a basic one for calls and texts makes far more sense than a full smartphone. And if they do have one, parents should set firm ground rules and keep a close eye on how it's being used. Everything in moderation, as they say.

questions.sampleAnswer:
The question of whether children under 12 should have smartphones is a highly contentious issue that divides parents, educators, and experts. Let me examine both sides of this debate.
Those who support restricting smartphones for young children raise several serious concerns. Firstly, smartphones can expose children to inappropriate content – violence, adult material, or harmful ideologies – that they're not mature enough to process. Secondly, excessive screen time has been linked to various health problems including eye strain, poor posture, and disrupted sleep patterns. Furthermore, social media platforms can lead to cyberbullying, anxiety, and depression among young users. Many argue that childhood should be spent playing outdoors and developing real-world social skills, not scrolling through feeds.
On the other hand, there are valid arguments for allowing children to have phones. Parents often cite safety concerns – being able to contact their child or track their location provides peace of mind. Additionally, many educational apps can enhance learning in engaging ways. In our digital world, some argue that children need to develop technological literacy early. Denying them access might leave them behind their peers.
In my opinion, a balanced approach works best. Perhaps children could use supervised devices with parental controls and time limits rather than unrestricted access. As the saying goes, "Everything in moderation." The key is teaching responsible use rather than complete prohibition.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
12 yoshgacha bo'lgan bolalarning smartfonga ega bo'lishi kerakmi degan savol ota-onalar, o'qituvchilar va mutaxassislarni ikkiga bo'lib yuboradigan juda bahsli masala hisoblanadi. Keling, ushbu bahsning har ikki tomonini ko'rib chiqaylik.

Yosh bolalar uchun smartfonlardan foydalanishni cheklashni qo'llab-quvvatlovchilar bir nechta jiddiy xavotirlarni ko'tarishadi. Birinchidan, smartfonlar bolalarni ularning aqliy rivojlanishi uchun yetarli bo'lmagan mos kelmaydigan kontentga – zo'ravonlik, kattalar uchun materiallar yoki zararli mafkuralarga duchor qilishi mumkin. Ikkinchidan, haddan tashqari ekran vaqti ko'zning zo'riqishi, noto'g'ri qomat va uyqu buzilishi kabi turli xil sog'liq muammolari bilan bog'liq. Bundan tashqari, ijtimoiy media platformalari yosh foydalanuvchilar orasida kiberbulling, tashvish va depressiyaga olib kelishi mumkin. Ko'pchilik bolalik davri ochiq havoda o'ynash va real dunyo ijtimoiy ko'nikmalarini rivojlantirishga sarflanishi kerak, degan fikrda.

Boshqa tomondan, bolalarga telefonlarga ega bo'lishga ruxsat berish uchun asosli dalillar mavjud. Ota-onalar ko'pincha xavfsizlik xavotirlarini ta'kidlashadi – farzandi bilan bog'lana olish yoki uning joylashuvini kuzatish xotirjamlikni ta'minlaydi. Bundan tashqari, ko'plab ta'limiy ilovalar qiziqarli usullar bilan o'rganishni yaxshilashi mumkin. Raqamli dunyomizda ba'zilar bolalar erta texnologik savodxonlikni rivojlantirishlari kerak deb hisoblashadi. Ularga kirishni rad etish tengdoshlaridan orqada qoldirishi mumkin.

Mening fikrimcha, muvozanatli yondashuv eng yaxshi ishlaydi. Ehtimol, bolalar cheklanmagan kirishdan ko'ra, ota-ona nazorati va vaqt cheklovlari bilan nazorat qilinadigan qurilmalardan foydalanishlari mumkin. Aytganidek, "Har narsaning me'yori bor". Asosiysi, to'liq taqiqlashdan ko'ra, mas'uliyatli foydalanishni o'rgatishdir.
